Android won\'t put ducker to sleep, so the VPN keeps working with the screen off.
Android may put ducker to sleep, and the VPN will drop when the screen is off.
On %1$s that\'s not enough: the phone\'s own system closes background apps.
%1$s phones close background apps, so the VPN may drop. It takes a minute to fix.
Tap “MIUI autostart” and turn ducker on in the list. Then “Battery: no restrictions” and choose No restrictions. And lock ducker in recent apps: pull its card down, or long-press it and tap the lock.
Open Phone Manager → App launch (on Huawei: Settings → Battery → App launch), find ducker, turn off automatic management and turn on all three switches. Then lock ducker in recent apps.
In ducker\'s app settings open Battery and allow unrestricted background use, then enable ducker in Apps → Autostart. Lock ducker in recent apps.

In Settings → Battery → Background power consumption allow ducker to run in the background, then enable ducker in Apps → Autostart (on older versions: i Manager → Autostart). Lock ducker in recent apps.

In ducker\'s app settings open Battery usage and allow background activity: on newer versions choose Allow background activity instead of Smart mode, on earlier ones turn on that switch and Allow auto launch. Then lock ducker in recent apps.
In ducker\'s app settings open Battery usage or Power saver and allow background running and auto launch. Then lock ducker in recent apps.

In Settings → Battery → Battery optimization choose Don\'t optimize for ducker, and turn off Advanced optimization in the extra settings there. Then lock ducker in recent apps: OnePlus sometimes turns optimization back on by itself.

In ducker\'s app settings open Battery and choose Unrestricted — if you allowed background work in ducker\'s prompt, this is already done. Then in Battery → Background usage limits make sure ducker is not among sleeping or deep sleeping apps.

In ducker\'s app settings open Battery and turn off battery optimization and putting the app to sleep. Then in Device care → Battery remove ducker from sleeping apps and turn off putting unused apps to sleep.

In ducker\'s app settings open Battery, turn on Allow background activity and choose Unrestricted. Then in App management open Auto-start and enable ducker. Lock ducker in recent apps: on these phones swiping it away stops the VPN.
Open Phone Master → Auto-start and allow ducker, then turn off power saving for apps in Settings → Battery. Lock ducker in recent apps.
When the screen turns off, Android puts apps to sleep and the VPN may drop. Let ducker run in the background — it barely affects battery: ducker never wakes the phone on its own.
Android will now ask about VPN

Android will warn that a VPN can monitor your traffic. It says this about every VPN, and the VPN can\'t start without your permission. Your traffic goes only to your subscription\'s servers; ducker itself collects and sends nothing. Allow the connection in that window.
Android no longer puts ducker to sleep, but the phone\'s own system still closes apps.
Android may put ducker to sleep, and the VPN will drop when the screen is off.
